title: Do Carbon Emissions Affect Stock Returns? Causal Evidence from a Supreme Court Ruling
authors: Xiaoyi Lyu; Chenyu Shan; Dragon Yongjun Tang
eligible_reason: Single event date (West Virginia v. EPA, June 30, 2022). Main tables are cross-sectional OLS of CARs on log emission intensity with firm controls (reg CAR_fm5_M30 ln_GHGscope1_intensity $control, r); the panel DiD uses post = (eventday >= 0) for every firm x highintens (or continuous ln intensity) with firm and event-day FE plus time-varying controls (reghdfe AR_fm5 c.post##c.highintens $control, absorb(id eventday)); EPS forecast and bond-spread regressions use postJun30 x ln intensity. One adoption date, no staggered binary treatment.
design_notes: Event study of stock returns around the June 30, 2022 Supreme Court ruling; placebo dates (Apr 29 2021, Jun 30 2021, Mar 31 2022, Jun 15 2022); heterogeneity by enforcement intensity, state climate policy (RPS/CES), institutional investors; analyst EPS forecasts and corporate bond spreads.
data_files_note: Cleaned analysis datasets (CRSP/Compustat/Trucost/I/B/E/S/TRACE derived) shipped; README does not describe any masking.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Single court-ruling date; not staggered.
